subject: Environment
description: UNEP, CITES, WWF, Greenpeace, Indian NGOs / agencies

questions.stem: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) has its headquarters in:
questions.explanation: UNEP — established after the 1972 Stockholm Conference — is HQed in Nairobi, Kenya, making it the first UN agency based in a developing country. Leads climate, biodiversity and pollution agendas; convenes the UN Environment Assembly (UNEA) every two years. Inger Andersen (Denmark) has been Executive Director since 2019.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) was signed in 1973 and entered into force in:
questions.explanation: CITES — signed 3 March 1973 in Washington DC (hence sometimes called the Washington Convention), came into force 1 July 1975. Classifies species into three Appendices — I (prohibition of commercial trade, e.g., tiger, elephant, rhino), II (regulated trade), III (regulated unilaterally by one country). India is a member since 1976. 3 March is observed as World Wildlife Day.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The well-known panda logo belongs to the organisation:
questions.explanation: WWF was founded in 1961 (Switzerland) and adopted the giant panda Chi-Chi (at London Zoo) as its logo. Works on biodiversity, climate, freshwater, oceans, food. Named originally World Wildlife Fund; renamed World Wide Fund for Nature in most countries in 1986 (US + Canada kept the older name). Greenpeace was founded in 1971 (Vancouver) around anti-nuclear-testing protests.

questions.stem: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) is a statutory body under which Indian ministry?

options.option_text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.explanation: CPCB — constituted 1974 under the Water Act — operates under MoEFCC. Sets national standards for air, water and noise; coordinates with the State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs); publishes the National Air Quality Index. Headquartered in Delhi.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: 'World Environment Day' is observed every year on:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day — observed on 5 June since 1974 (commemorating the 1972 Stockholm Conference). 2018 host — India; theme 'Beat Plastic Pollution'. Other climate-environment days: 22 April (Earth Day), 21 March (International Day of Forests), 22 May (Biodiversity Day), 8 June (World Oceans Day), 17 June (World Day to Combat Desertification and Drought), 16 September (World Ozone Day).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The 'Global Environment Facility' (GEF), which funds environmental projects in developing countries, was established in:
questions.explanation: GEF — established 1991 in advance of the Rio Earth Summit (1992) — pools funds from donor countries to support projects on climate, biodiversity, land degradation, international waters, persistent pollutants. Hosted by the World Bank but operationally independent. Complements the Adaptation Fund (under UNFCCC) and the Green Climate Fund (2010).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: 'Silent Spring', the 1962 book that spurred the modern environmental movement, was written by:
questions.explanation: Rachel Carson (American marine biologist / conservationist) wrote 'Silent Spring' (1962), exposing the dangers of DDT and other pesticides — especially their biomagnification up the food chain into fish-eating birds. Triggered the US ban on DDT (1972) and the founding of the EPA. Wangari Maathai — Kenyan, founded the Green Belt Movement, Nobel Peace 2004. Aldo Leopold — 'A Sand County Almanac'. Greta Thunberg — Swedish youth climate activist.
